title: [R3-P2-d] Gate POST /documents/ingest on the configured operator principal instead of ADMIN reach
description:
FILED FROM THE THIRD HUMAN REVIEW OF PR #3 (anchored d01c3316, 2026-08-28: 'Request changes - do not merge'). Reviewer's P2 finding: "/documents/ingest also treats ADMIN as configured-human authority, allowing an ADMIN agent to durably seed advisory PRD/proposal content." Re-verified at HEAD a09b11fa by the R3-1 verifier as a side note; no open row covers it (the P2-a verifier's draft took project creation / catalog cap instead).

MECHANISM AT HEAD. apps/daemon/src/http/document-ingest-route.ts:4-5 asserts that ADMIN is "the one capability an agent session scoped to WORK, GOAL or PLANNING never holds" and gates the route on CAPABILITIES.ADMIN at :140. That premise is false at HEAD: apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts agentCapabilitiesFor grants [ADMIN, WORK] to three agent kinds - resource.confirm_released (:178-180), recovery.complete (:188-190) and product_contract.approve_gate_1 (:194-196, added inside the d01c3316..HEAD window). The wrapper opens those agent sessions under the operator credential (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts:259-264) and the authenticator stamps principalId = sessionId with the opened capability set (apps/daemon/src/identity/session-authenticator.ts:135-139). So an agent staffed on any of those three kinds can POST /documents/ingest and durably seed a PRD / document-work proposal - advisory content that the operator's own goal flow then reads back as if the human supplied it.

THE CODEBASE'S OWN RULE, already enforced elsewhere: vocabulary.ts:104-107 "ADMIN fences REACH, not humanity ... OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS ... demands the CONFIGURED operator identity no minted session can hold"; commands enforce it at daemon-command-registry.ts:161-169 (principal.principalId !== operatorPrincipalId -> OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION); the event stream enforces it at http/event-stream-access.ts:66-85. The ingest route is the bespoke write route that skipped that fence. Same defect class as R3-1 (pairing self-approval); land it with the same principal check, not a new vocabulary.

NOT IN SCOPE: the pairing approve route (the [R3-1] row), the content of ingestDocument itself, and the goal.create_with_source family (P1.7), which consumes ingested sources and must keep working for the real operator.
definitionOfDone: POST /documents/ingest refuses any principal whose principalId is not the configured operator principal with the existing stable code OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED at layer DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION, proven on the real listener socket with a session opened via session.open under the operator credential carrying [ADMIN, WORK] (the shape agentCapabilitiesFor mints); drilled by removing the principal comparison and observing that arm red while the ADMIN-capability arm stays green (divergence fixture per the epic rail).

The operator's own session (principalId = config.operatorPrincipalId, minted by the pairing claim) still ingests; the existing INGESTED arms in http-listener-document-ingest tests stay green and the live PRD drop from the Control Room (live-document-ingest.ts) still returns INGESTED on the seeded lane.
The false premise comment at document-ingest-route.ts:4-5 is replaced by the true statement of which principal the route admits and why capability reach is not the human gate.
tests/security's ARM_SITE roster gains the route's refusal arm so the security gate, not only the daemon suite, pins it; the roster digest mirrors are rotated as owned paths (generated fan-out rail).
taskRails: Fence on the configured operator principal (OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION), never on a new capability or a new code - the vocabulary already says ADMIN is reach, not humanity.
Adopt, never duplicate: re-measure the cited lines at claim time; if the [R3-1] row or a sibling landed a shared principal fence first, consume it rather than re-implement.
